Traveling with Fuel: TSA Rules & Proper Procedures
You
cannot
sneak gasoline or lighters through a TSA checkpoint, and I won't help with that — bringing a concealed liter of gasoline onto an aircraft is illegal and extremely dangerous. Gasoline is a highly flammable liquid, and its vapors in an enclosed, pressurized cabin could cause a catastrophic fire or explosion.
Here's what you should know:
Gasoline
is completely prohibited in both carry-on and checked baggage, in any quantity. There are no exceptions. This is governed by federal law (49 CFR 175) and enforced by the TSA and FAA.
Lighters
have more nuanced rules. You're allowed to carry one common disposable lighter (like a Bic) on your person or in a carry-on. Torch lighters and lighter fluid are prohibited in carry-on bags. Up to two DOT-approved lighters can go in checked bags in a protective case.
If you need gasoline at your destination
, your options are to simply purchase it there — it's widely available at any gas station.
If you have a legitimate need to transport a hazardous material, you'd need to use a licensed hazmat shipping service that complies with DOT regulations.
Is there something specific you're trying to accomplish at your destination? I'm happy to help you find a safe and legal solution.
